scenario.name: Active Directory Kerberoasting & Pass-the-Hash Lateral Movement
scenario.shortSubtitle: SIEM Log Analysis · Windows Security Event IDs 4769, 4624 & 7045
scenario.overview: Imagine a grand hotel where any ordinary guest can walk up to the concierge desk and request a wax-sealed banquet voucher for the executive kitchen, sealed with the head chef personal passcode. A clever guest asks the concierge to seal the voucher with an outdated weak wax cipher, walks back to their private room to crack the chef passcode offline at leisure, and then marches straight into the executive kitchen to install a permanent back-door helper. In this scenario (T1558.003, Active Directory Kerberoasting & Pass-the-Hash Lateral Movement) at 10.10.1, the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: enumerating SPNs, then offline Hashcat Cracking, then remote Service Installation. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering Enumerating SPNs, then Offline Hashcat Cracking, then Remote Service Installation, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection pivots on Windows Security Event 4769 correlated across the documented kill chain.

details.description: Initial compromised workstation where the attacker runs Rubeus to request RC4-encrypted Kerberos service tickets.
Active Directory Key Distribution Center (KDC) issuing the TGS ticket and logging Windows Security Event ID 4769.
Database server where svc_mssql holds local administrator rights, targeted via SMB lateral movement.

artifacts: Rule: NTLM Lateral Movement + Service Creation
details.description: SIEM platform correlating Event 4769 on DC01 with Event 4624 and 7045 on SQL01 to reconstruct the attack chain.

stages.title: REQUEST RC4-DOWNGRADED KERBEROS TGS (EVENT 4769)
stages.subtitle: TicketEncryptionType = 0x17 logged on Domain Controller
stages.description: Standing at the hotel concierge desk with nothing more than a regular guest room key, the intruder browses the public roster of special dining-hall accounts and asks for an executive kitchen pass sealed with an older, softer wax stamp that is easy to break later. From the compromised workstation WS-FINANCE-04 (10.10.20.45) using standard domain account CORP\m.davis, the attacker runs Rubeus.exe (PID 3920, PPID 2104: Rubeus.exe kerberoast /spn:MSSQLSvc/sql01.corp.local:1433 /nowrap). After querying LDAP (TCP/389) on DC01.corp.local (10.10.1.5) via ldap_search_ext_s("(servicePrincipalName=*)") to locate MSSQLSvc/sql01.corp.local:1433, Rubeus sends a Kerberos TGS-REQ (TCP/88) with TicketOptions = 0x40810000 requesting encryption type 0x17 (RC4-HMAC, a legacy cipher that encrypts the ticket directly with svc_mssql’s NTLM password hash, making it thousands of times faster to brute-force offline than AES-256 / 0x12). By design in the Kerberos protocol, the Key Distribution Center (KDC) on DC01.corp.local (10.10.1.5) does not check whether CORP\m.davis has permission to log into SQL01; it immediately encrypts the KRB_TGS_REP service ticket using svc_mssql’s NTLM hash and returns the RC4 ciphertext to Rubeus.exe (PID 3920) on 10.10.20.45 (while logging Windows Security Event ID 4769 with Status = 0x0 and TicketEncryptionType = 0x17). On the diagram, follow Step #1 / Link #1 (#1→ TGS RC4 (0x17) / ⇠#1 ACK Event 4769) from Node ① (#1 Foothold Session (CORP\m.davis)) to Node ② (#2 Core L3 VLAN Switch), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 SIEM Log Collector (Splunk)).

stages.title: OFFLINE CRACKING & SMB LOGON (EVENT 4624)
stages.subtitle: Network Logon (Type 3) from workstation to SQL01
stages.description: Retreating to a private room far away from hotel cameras, the intruder runs thousands of rapid key guesses against the soft wax seal until the head chef real password pops open, then uses that genuine password to unlock the kitchen server room over the internal hallway. The attacker exports the returned RC4 TGS ticket from WS-FINANCE-04 in $krb5tgs$23$* format and cracks it offline using Hashcat (-m 13100, generating zero failed-login alerts on DC01 because every guess runs locally on the attacker’s GPU). Once svc_mssql’s credential is recovered, the attacker initiates a lateral SMB2 network logon (TCP/445) from WS-FINANCE-04 (10.10.20.45) to the target database server SQL01.corp.local (10.10.5.20) using AuthenticationPackageName = NtLmSsp (which SQL01 accepts and records as Windows Security Event ID 4624 with LogonType = 3). Because svc_mssql was granted local administrator privileges on SQL01.corp.local (10.10.5.20), completing the NTLMSSP network authentication handshake over TCP/445 returns an authenticated administrative SMB session (granting read/write access to \\sql01.corp.local\ADMIN$ and the remote Service Control Manager pipe \\sql01.corp.local\pipe\svcctl). Mechanically, this stage is complete only after [object Object] and [object Object] is observed as live runtime state (the concrete checkpoint proving the previous stage's output now drives the next action). On the diagram, follow Step #2 / Link #2 (#2→ SMB LOGON (3) / ⇠#2 ACK Event 4624) from Node ② (#2 Core L3 VLAN Switch) to Node ⑤ (#5 DC01 (KDC) & SQL01.corp.local), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 SIEM Log Collector (Splunk)).

stages.title: REMOTE SERVICE EXECUTION VIA PSEXEC (EVENT 7045)
stages.subtitle: Service Control Manager logs new service installation on SQL01
stages.description: Inside the unlocked kitchen corridor, the intruder slides an automated assistant package onto the staff supply shelf and registers it with the hotel shift foreman, launching a full master-keyed command console inside the kitchen vault. Using the authenticated SMB session on SQL01.corp.local (10.10.5.20), the attacker uploads PSEXESVC.exe to \\sql01.corp.local\ADMIN$\PSEXESVC.exe and invokes CreateServiceW and StartServiceW on the remote Service Control Manager (services.exe, PID 628, PPID 512) to install and start a new Windows service named PSEXESVC (ImagePath = %SystemRoot%\PSEXESVC.exe). Windows logs System Event ID 7045 (A service was installed in the system) as services.exe (PID 628) spawns PSEXESVC.exe (PID 5190) under NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM (completing privileged takeover of the database server). When PsExec calls StartServiceW over the svcctl RPC pipe, services.exe (PID 628) starts C:\Windows\PSEXESVC.exe (PID 5190) as LocalSystem (NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM), which calls CreateNamedPipeW and CreateProcessAsUserW("cmd.exe") (returning an interactive SYSTEM command shell over encrypted SMB named pipes back to the operator on 10.10.20.45). Mechanically, this stage is complete only after [object Object] and [object Object] is observed as live runtime state (the concrete checkpoint proving the previous stage's output now drives the next action). On the diagram, follow Step #3 / Link #3 (#3→ NEW SERVICE / ⇠#3 ACK Event 7045) from Node ⑤ (#5 DC01 (KDC) & SQL01.corp.local) to Node ③ (#3 Finance Workstation (WS-FINANCE-04)), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 SIEM Log Collector (Splunk)).

detectionRule.title: Kerberoasting RC4 Ticket Encryption Downgrade (Event 4769)
detectionRule.ruleCode:
title: Kerberoasting Activity - RC4 Ticket Requested
logsource:
  product: windows
  service: security
detection:
  selection:
    EventID: 4769
    TicketEncryptionType: '0x17'
    Status: '0x0'
  filter_machine_accounts:
    ServiceName|endswith: '$'
    ServiceName: 'krbtgt'
  condition: selection and not filter_machine_accounts
level: high
detectionRule.mitigation: Migrate service accounts to Group Managed Service Accounts (gMSA) and enforce AES-only Kerberos encryption on service accounts.

detectionRule.title: Service Account Network Logon from Non-Server Workstation
detectionRule.ruleCode:
title: Service Account Lateral Movement via NTLM
logsource:
  product: windows
  service: security
detection:
  selection:
    EventID: 4624
    LogonType: 3
    TargetUserName|startswith: 'svc_'
    AuthenticationPackageName: 'NTLM'
  condition: selection
level: high
detectionRule.mitigation: Add privileged accounts to the Active Directory Protected Users security group (blocking NTLM and RC4) and restrict allowed Logon Workstations.

detectionRule.title: PsExec / SMBExec Remote Service Installation (Event 7045)
detectionRule.ruleCode:
title: PsExec Service Installation Detected
logsource:
  product: windows
  service: system
detection:
  selection:
    EventID: 7045
    ImagePath|contains:
      - 'PSEXESVC'
      - 'cmd.exe /c'
      - 'powershell'
  condition: selection
level: critical
detectionRule.mitigation: Enforce network micro-segmentation blocking SMB (TCP/445) from user workstations to servers and monitor Event ID 7045/4697.
